facts.text: The white-browed woodswallow is a medium-sized Australian bird with a white brow over a black head, blue-grey upper body and chestnut underparts.
facts.quote: The white-browed woodswallow has very distinctive plumage consisting of white brow over a black head with the upper body being a deep blue-grey and with a chestnut under body.

facts.text: It has a divided tongue, like most woodswallows.
facts.quote: The white-browed woodswallow has a bifurcated (divided) tongue like most woodswallows.

facts.text: Highly nomadic, it travels in flocks ranging from hundreds to thousands of birds.
facts.quote: White-browed woodswallows are highly nomadic travelling in pairs to flocks from hundred to thousands of birds.

facts.text: It often heads north for winter and returns south in spring to nest, regularly mixing with masked woodswallows.
facts.quote: They often wander irregularly around inland Australia, usually heading north for winter in the Northern Territory and central Queensland, and south in spring for nesting. White-browed woodswallows regularly associate with flocks of the masked woodswallow Artamus personatus.

facts.text: It mainly eats insects but will feed on nectar when blossoms are available.
facts.quote: White-browed woodswallows feed on nectar when blossoms are available but mainly feed on insects.

facts.text: It nests in shrubs, tree forks, hollow stumps or posts, building a nest of twigs, grass and rootlets.
facts.quote: The species nests in shrubs, forks of trees, hollow stumps or posts, the nest is usually made of twigs, grass and rootlets.

facts.text: It lives in places ranging from rainforest margins and woodlands to golf courses, vineyards and suburban streets.
facts.quote: They inhabit margins of rainforests, woodlands, inland/coastal scrubs, golf courses, vineyards, suburban streets and arid areas of Australia.

facts.text: It makes a 'tchip-tchip' call similar to masked woodswallows.
facts.quote: They make a 'tchip-tchip' call similar to masked woodswallows.
